findings.title: Core public-flow acceptance criterion is still unproven because accepted relay OK is not asserted anywhere
evidence: TPG-AC-002 requires a representative public signer-first browser flow to "require at least one accepted OK response" before completion.
TPG-T-002 in test_matrix.json is still `not_implemented` with failure reason: the existing public smoke does not record accepted relay OK responses or assert that accepted OK is required.
verification_report.md marks TPG-AC-002 only `partial` and repeats that accepted relay OK handling is not asserted by the current harness.
web/tests/e2e/service-deployment-public-smoke.spec.js only checks request kinds, relay URLs, intent/run counts, and resulting UI state; it never inspects relay OK responses.
findings.suggested_action: Do not treat the current public smoke as sufficient proof. Extend the public harness and smoke test to record publish OK frames and assert that a public workflow does not count as complete without at least one accepted relay OK.

findings.title: Verification overclaims encrypted completion coverage: relay-close failure path is claimed but not exercised
evidence: TPG-T-014 in test_matrix.json says the encrypted completion proof should exercise decrypt-failure and relay-close paths.
verification_report.md marks TPG-AC-011 as pass on the basis that TPG-T-013 and TPG-T-014 are passing, and describes encrypted completion as grounded in explicit result/decrypt/relay-close signals.
web/src/lib/nostr/encrypted-controlplane.js contains an `onClosed` branch in `awaitEncryptedResult(...)` that rejects when all relays close or when the close reason implies auth.

web/tests/unit/encrypted-controlplane.test.js has no `onClosed` match at all and no test that invokes the subscription close handler; the current passing suite proves accepted/rejected publish and decrypt failure, but not relay-close failure behavior.
findings.suggested_action: Downgrade the current claim or add explicit unit coverage for relay-close failure handling (including all-relays-closed and auth-related close reasons) before continuing to cite TPG-T-014 as full evidence for AC-011.

findings.title: Browser log-transport contract is underspecified, so the planned EventSource-exclusion proof can be gamed by scanning too little
evidence: TPG-AC-007 says "A first-party browser log experience covered by this transport-policy slice" must not require EventSource-based `streamLogs(...)`, but it does not enumerate which browser log surfaces are in scope.

TPG-T-009 in test_matrix.json proposes a contract test over an "approved browser slice module allowlist", but no allowlist artifact exists in the feature folder and the target test file does not exist yet.
verification_report.md already acknowledges that the dedicated EventSource-exclusion proof does not exist and keeps TPG-AC-007 at `not_verified`.
Without a stable in-scope surface list, a future contract test could pass by checking only a narrow subset of modules while missing a real browser log path that still depends on EventSource.
findings.suggested_action: Before implementing TPG-T-009, define the exact browser log surfaces that belong to this feature slice and treat that list as a durable artifact or explicit test input.

proposed_hitl_question.question: Which browser log surfaces are in scope for TPG-AC-007 in this transport-policy slice?
options: Only deployment run-log retrieval surfaces already governed by encrypted log flows
All first-party browser log viewers, including any service log pages that still use streamLogs/EventSource
Only settings/admin log surfaces for this release
Defer browser log-surface classification and remove TPG-AC-007 from this release gate

findings.title: Settings relay-visibility path is still proving the wrong transport boundary and remains a live blocker
evidence: TPG-AC-010 requires operator-facing relay visibility to come from a service-authored NIP-51 kind `30002` relay-list event rather than raw `systemInfo.nostr.relays` discovery data.
web/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte` still renders `systemInfo.nostr.relays` directly under the "Server Relays" row.
defects.json keeps TPG-D-002 open at severity `major` with recommended fix to replace raw discovery fields with a kind `30002` relay-list path.
HITL-TRANSPORT_POLICY_GOVERNANCE-005 explicitly classifies TPG-D-002 as `BLOCKER`, and verification_report.md keeps TPG-AC-010 at `fail` with TPG-T-012 not implemented.
findings.suggested_action: Treat the settings page as a release blocker until it is rewired to the service-authored relay-list event and a deterministic e2e proof exists for that path.

findings.title: Confidence scoring masks unverified must-level ACs by awarding full AC coverage for linked-but-unproven tests
evidence: confidence_report.json assigns `acceptance_criteria_coverage.score = 1.0` because all 12 must-level ACs have at least one linked test row.
verification_report.md simultaneously reports TPG-AC-002 and TPG-AC-004 as `partial`, TPG-AC-007 and TPG-AC-012 as `not_verified`, and TPG-AC-010 as `fail`.
Five linked required tests are still `not_implemented`: TPG-T-002, TPG-T-005, TPG-T-009, TPG-T-012, and TPG-T-015.

The report status remains `needs_patch`, but the 1.0 AC-coverage component can still mislead a downstream reader into believing the must-level contract is fully evidenced rather than merely fully mapped.
findings.suggested_action: Keep the current overall status blocked, but consider adding a second AC-evidence metric or explicit cap for failing/unverified must-level ACs so future confidence reports do not present full linkage as full proof.
